summary: Provision the sandbox so remote verification is actually possible instead of degrading the release gate: allow the git host explicitly via `sandbox.network.allowedDomains` (e.g. `*.github.com`), and keep the token usable without exposing it by masking it — `credentials.envVars` entry for `GH_TOKEN` with `mode: "mask"` and `injectHosts: ["api.github.com"]` plus `network.tlsTerminate` — set from user/managed settings or `--settings` (repository settings are ignored for masks); on hosted web/cloud sessions use the built-in git proxy, which keeps credentials outside the sandbox and restricts push to the working branch.

evidence.summary: Documents sandbox.network.allowedDomains, credentials.envVars mask with injectHosts and the network.tlsTerminate requirement, notes that mask entries are honored only from user settings, managed settings or --settings, and that a plain deny on GITHUB_TOKEN 'breaks tools that need it, such as gh' (masking requires v2.1.199+).

Hosted sessions limit network to allowlisted domains and hand git a scoped credential that the proxy translates to the real GitHub token, enabling clone/fetch/PR operations while restricting push to the current working branch.

Reports git operations failing silently with exit code 128 under the sandbox because github.com is not allowlisted and no whitelist prompt is offered — the failure mode presents as an unexplained capability gap.

conditions: Agent runs inside Claude Code's Bash sandbox or a hosted web/cloud session that must reach a git remote or the GitHub API
The operator controls user or managed settings for the environment
Workflows whose correctness depends on comparing against a remote authority base or opening a PR
not_applicable_when: Environments with deliberate air-gapping or an organization policy of no outbound egress — there the correct response is the fail-closed gate (RMD-AUTHGATE-001), not widening egress
Repositories where the agent must not hold push capability at all

expected_effect.primary: The remote authority base becomes reachable and PR creation becomes possible from inside the sandbox, so runs are planned and recorded against a verified remote head rather than an unverifiable local head — removing the pressure that drove the delivery gate to be loosened.

risks: Security-boundary change (local risk tier R3): must be reviewed by a human and never auto-applied by the closed loop
Masking authorizes the proxy to send the real credential to the listed hosts; a wrong injectHosts entry widens exposure
Without network.tlsTerminate, masking fails closed and authentication silently breaks
Allowlisting a broad wildcard domain grants more egress than the workflow needs
revalidate_when: Claude Code changes sandbox network or credential-masking settings
The hosted session git-proxy behavior or branch-push restriction changes
A run again records authority_base.reachable false after the settings are provisioned
